title: Give ChatGPT and Claude the Same Memory
lesson: A remembered object can be asked for in another model; the edit teaches this through a same-object input/response test, then a shared-memory model.
opening: Presenter promises cross-model memory; a typed app name and terminal-stack Memory graphic quickly label the endpoints and concept.
story_arc: Promise → repeated-context inconvenience → create/connect/remember → ask the same object in ChatGPT → returned guideline card → shared-center explanation → control assurances and testimony → link CTA.
payoff: The returned asset card pays off the same-object question. Encryption and model-specific access are asserted but not demonstrated; late coding/shopping footage does not close that gap.
selection_reason: Shows a useful input→same-object→returned-artifact chain, a real whole-diagram enlargement and hold, and the difference between concrete demonstration and generic technical B-roll.
review_limits: All four chronological 0.5s sheets (76 sampled frames) were visually opened, plus six 6fps strips. This is full-duration sampled coverage, not every source frame reviewed. Video is 1080x1920/60fps; no audio audition. Spoken ideas use machine VTT alignment and visible captions; tail overrun is excluded from exact timing claims. Motion observations do not establish easing. Product/security assertions and catalog replica readiness are not verified.
